book.name: Kids on Bikes
book.tagline: Second Edition — collaborative storytelling in small towns full of big adventure.
book.blurb: A rules-light, fast-paced roleplaying game about ordinary kids, teens and adults in a small town who stumble into strange, creepy mysteries — and about the Powered Character the whole table shares control of. Six Stats rated d4–d20, Tropes to build from, Strengths, Flaws, Adversity Tokens, Lucky Breaks, and a bike you love.

ageGroups.name: Child
ageGroups.notes: Cannot take Rebellious. Quick and generally likable. Almost no access to money.

ageGroups.name: Teen
ageGroups.notes: Pugnacious and in their prime. Limited access to money.

ageGroups.name: Adult
ageGroups.notes: The Skilled at… skill usually reflects a job or a long-honed talent. Can buy what they need, within reason.

rules: Pick a Trope (Appendix C) or build from scratch: assign d20/d12/d10/d8/d6/d4 to the six Stats.
Age gives +1 to two Stats' checks and one free Strength; then choose two more Strengths and one Flaw.
Start with 3 Adversity Tokens (AT). Failing a check earns 1 AT; each AT spent adds +1 to a roll (yours or a friend's in the scene).
Rolling a die's maximum is a Lucky Break: reroll and add. AT never trigger Lucky Breaks.
Planned Actions may take half the die's maximum instead of rolling; Snap Decisions must be rolled.
One Knack at start (take a 10 once per session instead of rolling); never more than 3 Knacks, and never more than 4 Knacks + Bonded Actions combined.
Choose a bike: a Color (adjective + benefit) and one Upgrade (Appendix J), or take your Trope's gift bike.
The Powered Character is introduced by the GM in the first session and co-controlled by everyone through Aspects; powers run on a pool of 7 Power Tokens (d6 per PT).
Harm is resolved in a single contested check after everyone agrees to the stakes; violence only between characters in the same age bracket or within two years of age.

strengths.name: Cool Under Pressure
strengths.description: May spend 1 Adversity Token to take half of your die's value instead of rolling on a Snap Decision.

strengths.name: Easygoing
strengths.description: Gain 2 Adversity Tokens when you fail, instead of 1.

strengths.name: Gross
strengths.description: You have some kind of gross bodily trick (loud, quiet, smelly… up to you) that you can do on command.

strengths.name: Heroic
strengths.description: You do not need the GM's permission to spend Adversity Tokens to ignore Fears.

strengths.name: Intuitive
strengths.description: May spend 1 Adversity Token to ask the GM about your surroundings, an NPC, or the like. The GM must answer honestly.

strengths.name: Loyal
strengths.description: Each of the Adversity Tokens you spend to help your friends gives them a +2 instead of a +1.

strengths.name: Lucky
strengths.description: You may spend 2 Adversity Tokens to reroll a stat check.

strengths.name: Prepared
strengths.description: May spend 2 Adversity Tokens to just happen to have one commonplace item with you (GM's discretion).

strengths.name: Protective
strengths.description: Add +3 to rolls when defending one of your friends.

strengths.name: Quick Healing
strengths.description: (Free for kids; available to teens and adults) You recover from injuries more quickly, and don't suffer lasting effects from most injuries.

strengths.name: Rebellious
strengths.description: (Free for and available only to teens) Add +3 to rolls to persuade or resist persuasion from Kids. Add +3 to rolls to resist persuasion from Adults.

strengths.name: Skilled at…
strengths.description: (Free for Adults; available to teens and, at GM's discretion, to kids) Choose a skill (GM's discretion). You are assumed to succeed when making even moderately difficult checks involving this skill. If the GM determines that you do need to roll for a more difficult check, add up to +3 to your roll.

strengths.name: Tough
strengths.description: If you lose a combat roll, add +3 to the negative number. You will still lose the roll no matter what but could reduce your loss to -1.

strengths.name: Treasure Hunter
strengths.description: May spend 1 Adversity Token to find a useful item in your surroundings.

strengths.name: Unassuming
strengths.description: May spend 2 Adversity Tokens to not be seen, within reason (GM's discretion).

strengths.name: Wealthy
strengths.description: May spend money as though you were in a higher age bracket. A wealthy child has the disposable income of a typical teen, and a wealthy teen that of a typical adult. A wealthy adult doesn't have to worry too much about money—they can buy anything they need, and likely spend their way out of a lot of situations.

questions.text: Why do you feel forever indebted to this character?
What do you secretly admire about this character?
What great kindness did this character do for you that they did without thinking about it—but that meant the world to you?
What part of this character's personality do you realize is exceptional that they do not?
In what way do you care for them that they can't or won't reciprocate?
How did this character contribute to the best day of your life?
What plan do you and this character have that most excites you?
What is your private nickname for this character and why?
When did this character surprise you with how far they'd go to help you?
What are you sacrificing to protect this character, and why are you so willing to make that sacrifice?
You often feel the need to stand up for this character. Why are you willing to go so far for them?
What bond do you share with this character that can never be broken?
What about this character makes you so happy?
What tremendous act of bravery did you see this character do?
What do you and this character have a mutual love of that no one else in town seems to like?
You recently thought you lost this character. How? Why was that so upsetting?
What aspect of this character's personality do you try to use as a model for your own?
When did you first realize that you loved this character—either platonically or romantically?
You've been in awe of this character since you met them. How did they make such a strong first impression?
Why do you treasure a seemingly valueless item this character once gave you?
What did this character once do that you still resent them for?
What secret are you keeping from them, and who would be devastated if they found out?
You're sure this character is hiding something from you. How do you feel knowing they're deceiving you?
What does this character have that you want to take from them?
This character regularly does something that hurts you, perhaps without knowing it. What is it, and why do you think they keep doing it?
How did this character contribute to the worst day of your life?
What dishonest thing did you see this character do that still bothers you to this day?
How does this character keep putting you both at risk? Why do you think they do that?
What does this character often do that makes you irrationally angry?
How do you think this character is self-sabotaging? Why can't you empathize?
What part of this character's personality scares you? What does that say about you?
You can't forgive this character for something they did. What is it and why can't you?
What dangerous behavior has this character recently started engaging in? How could it affect you?
What is your plan to get revenge on this character, and what misunderstanding led you to make this plan?
Why do you dislike this character when most of the town seems to love them?
You hurt this character years ago. Why can't you apologize?
What do you intentionally do to annoy this character? What do you get from their response?
How did this character betray you the last time you confided in them?
This character hurt someone close to you. Why haven't you accepted their apology even though the person they hurt has?
What do you owe this character? Why do you refuse to repay them?
What good thing have you heard about this character that you can't believe is true?
Why do some members of the town seek out this character?
Recently, this character did something great for the town. Why was it so surprising?
What charming habit is this character known for throughout the town?
What strange record does this character hold in the town?
Why is this character's family so important in the town?
Which influential townsperson always speaks highly of this character and why?
Based on what you know, how is this character different from the rest of their family?
Why are you going out of your way to get to know this character?
What bad thing have you heard about this character that you can't believe is true?
What do you selfishly hope to gain from this relative stranger?
What bad reputation does this character have around the town?
Who does this character have a very public feud with?
Why are so many townspeople afraid of this character?
What do you want out of this relationship for your own selfish benefit?
How is this character threatening their family's reputation?
What scandal in the town was this character involved with?
How did you embarrass yourself last time you tried to get to know this character?
What rumor is whispered about this character around the town?
You know that this character is interested in getting to know you. How did you find that out?

items.name: Green

items.name: Neon Pink
items.benefit: You get +1 to Flight checks.

items.name: Orange
items.benefit: Each time you succeed at a check, an ally of your choice receives one Adversity Token.

items.name: Purple
items.benefit: You may treat Snap Decisions as Planned Actions.

items.name: Red
items.benefit: Each Adversity Token you spend during a check adds an additional +1 to your roll.

items.name: Rusty
items.benefit: You get +1 to Grit checks.

items.name: Silver
items.benefit: You have the Protective strength.

items.name: White
items.benefit: You get +1 to Brains checks.

items.name: Banana Seat
items.benefit: Your bike can carry a passenger. Once per day, if the Powered Character is your passenger, they regain up to 2 PT. (This cannot put them over their starting amount.)

items.name: Basket
items.benefit: Once per day, you may reach into the basket and come up with a commonplace item.

items.name: Bell
items.benefit: If you can explain, in narrative terms, how ringing the bell helps an ally during their check, they get +1 to that check.

items.name: First-Aid Kit
items.benefit: Once per day, you may use this first-aid kit to help an ally recover from an injury (at GM's discretion).

items.name: Milk Crate
items.benefit: Your bike can carry a single large item. You must explain, in narrative terms, why your bike is outfitted to carry this item.

items.name: Pegs
items.benefit: Your bike can carry a passenger. If you have a passenger, they receive the benefits of your bike's color as well.

items.name: Tassels
items.benefit: You get +1 to all checks while being chased.

items.name: Ten Speeder
items.benefit: You may shift into a lower gear and pedal hard to add d4 to your Flight checks, but you suffer -1 to all Brawn and Grit checks until you can fully catch your breath.

items.name: Trading Cards
items.benefit: You get +1 to checks if you are attempting to distract others.

items.name: Pedal-Powered Lights
items.benefit: You get +1 to all checks after dark.

Brains.text: How book-smart a character is: how well they understand problems, how they do in school, and how quickly they solve intellectual puzzles.

Brawn.text: How much brute strength a character has — not how well they fight, but how well they lift things, how athletic they are, and how physically intimidating.

Fight.text: How scary your character is, in and out of a fight. They learn to fight or use weapons more easily, and look like they can handle themselves if things get physical.

Flight.text: How fast a character is and how skilled they are at evading their problems, literally or figuratively — quick legs and quick mouths.

Charm.text: How socially adept a character is and how well they read the emotions of others. High Charm talks its way out of tough situations and into good ones.

Grit.text: How hard it is to unsettle a character emotionally or physically. High Grit keeps a level head in the worst situations, and it also covers street smarts.

dice.label: Superb
dice.text: Even upon first meeting you, anyone would readily tell this is a strength of yours. You are remarkably good with respect to this stat.

dice.label: Impressive
dice.text: People who know you would say you're pretty good with respect to this stat, but it wouldn't be obvious during a first encounter.

dice.label: Above Average
dice.text: You aren't remarkably good in terms of this stat, but you're slightly above average.

dice.label: Below Average
dice.text: You aren't too bad in terms of this stat, but you're certainly not good, either. Just slightly worse than average.

dice.label: Bad
dice.text: People who know you would say you're pretty bad with respect to this stat, but it wouldn't be obvious during a first encounter.

dice.label: Terrible
dice.text: Upon first meeting you, people would immediately tell this is a weakness of yours. You are remarkably bad with respect to this stat.

difficulties.text: A task at which only the most incredible could even possibly succeed—one of the most impressive things a character has ever done. Nearly guaranteed failure.
difficulties.examples: Lifting a car off of someone trapped under it; solving a nearly impossible math problem just by glancing at it.

difficulties.text: A task where success would be incredible and impressive. This, too, is a nearly guaranteed failure.
difficulties.examples: Talking a police officer out of arresting you when you have clearly broken the law and have no relationship with the officer; breaking a school record in track.

difficulties.text: A task where success is extraordinary—but decidedly possible for those who are truly skilled at it.
difficulties.examples: Doing a flying side kick into the center of a wildly swinging punching bag; withstanding a police interrogation.

difficulties.text: A task where success is impressive—but unsurprising for those skilled at it.
difficulties.examples: A strong person prying open a heavy, locked door; a computer whiz repairing a computer quickly under pressure.

difficulties.text: A task where success is almost certain for those very skilled at it—but not for those who aren't.
difficulties.examples: Convincing the principal that it wasn't you and your friends who started the cafeteria food fight; running a message from one end of a building to the other in a very short time.

difficulties.text: A task where success is likely for all but those who aren't skilled or have a low stat in that field.
difficulties.examples: Throwing a good punch into a punching bag; a character silently withstanding a verbal berating.

difficulties.text: A task where success is nearly guaranteed, except in extreme cases.
difficulties.examples: Lifting a 10-pound weight over their head; reciting a multiplication table.

adversity.name: Earning AT
adversity.text: Failing a check earns 1 Adversity Token (2 with Easygoing). Failing because you acted on your Flaw earns an additional AT. Tiered checks never earn AT. Everyone starts with 3 AT.

adversity.name: Improve a roll
adversity.text: After rolling, spend AT to add +1 each to your result (+2 each with Loyal when helping). Characters in the same scene may spend AT on your roll. Explain how past difficulties prepared you, or what advice you give.

adversity.name: Activate a Strength
adversity.text: Many Strengths have an AT cost listed in their description; pay it to use the effect.

adversity.name: Ignore a Fear
adversity.text: With the GM's permission (or the Heroic Strength), spend 1 AT per -1 of Fear penalty before rolling to ignore all three effects of the Fear for the scene.

adversity.name: No Lucky Breaks from AT
adversity.text: Spending AT never causes a Lucky Break; only a natural maximum roll does.

quickRules.title: Stat Checks
quickRules.text: Agree a Stat with the GM, who sets a difficulty. Roll that Stat die, add bonuses (age, Strengths, bike) and subtract Fear penalties. Meet or beat the difficulty to succeed. Max natural roll is 20, but difficulties can go higher.

quickRules.title: Lucky Breaks
quickRules.text: Roll the die's maximum value: roll it again and add. Keep going on repeated maximums. Narrate the success as something beyond what you could do alone.

quickRules.title: Adversity Tokens
quickRules.text: Start with 3. Earn 1 when you fail a check (2 with Easygoing; +1 more if the failure came from acting on your Flaw). Spend after rolling for +1 each on your roll or a friend's in the scene, to activate Strengths, or (with permission) to ignore Fears.

quickRules.title: Planned vs Snap
quickRules.text: Planned Actions happen with time and calm: you may take half the die's maximum instead of rolling. Snap Decisions are quick choices under pressure: you must roll. The GM decides which; players can argue for a moment of calm.

quickRules.title: Knacks
quickRules.text: Once per session, take a 10 on a check your Knack covers instead of rolling. Phrase it as an '-ing' verb and apply it creatively but sensibly. Start with 1; never more than 3, and never more than 4 Knacks and Bonded Actions combined.

quickRules.title: Tiered Checks
quickRules.text: When failure is impossible (racing, searching with all afternoon), the roll only decides how much you get. No consequences, but no Adversity Token either.

quickRules.title: Degrees of Success
quickRules.text: Compare roll + modifiers to the target: +10 or more is effortless with possible bonuses; +5 to +9 impressive; +1 to +4 plain success; 0 skin-of-the-teeth; -1 to -4 minor short-term trouble; -5 to -9 bad but manageable; -10 to -14 profound; -15 or lower staggering and long-lasting.

quickRules.title: Doing Harm
quickRules.text: Any attempt to harm resolves in a single contested check. The instigator names the harm and Stat; the GM sets inescapable consequences for the group (if a PC instigates); each side says what they risk and hope to gain; roll; the higher roller narrates who wins and who loses — at least one character gives up what they risked.

quickRules.title: Fears
quickRules.text: When your Fear is present: all checks are Snap Decisions (even with a Knack); you can't spend AT to help friends (they can still help you); and the GM may apply up to -3 (-1 persistent but irrelevant, -2 persistent and relevant, -3 overwhelming). Brief instances only affect a check or two.

quickRules.title: Motivations & Obligations
quickRules.text: A Motivation drives your big decisions (specific, general, or something to conceal). Obligations are what you must do — chores, work, family, keeping up appearances. No mechanics; they give the GM hooks and you a lens.

quickRules.title: Backpack
quickRules.text: The items you're never without (bag, locker, or car trunk for adults) plus the figurative advantages you carry — supportive parents, self-reliance, a grandmother's advice. Intangibles have no mechanics but suggest where to turn for help.

quickRules.title: Bikes
quickRules.text: Choose a Color (adjective + benefit while riding) and one Upgrade (two-word phrase + benefit), or take your Trope's gift bike. Name it, say how you got it and your favorite memory. Upgrades can be gained or lost between arcs; a bike always keeps at least one bonus.

quickRules.title: Bonded Actions
quickRules.text: Optional: two characters who know each other well pick one shared trick (Appendix I), usable once per session when both can actually help and it fits their backstory (give three shared experiences). No more than one Bonded Action with the same character.

quickRules.title: Relationship Questions
quickRules.text: Roll a d20 on the Positive or Negative list for characters you know, or the Don't Know list for those you don't. Reroll or pick an adjacent question if it doesn't fit or was already used. Quick start: one question about one character; complete: two per known character, one per unknown.

quickRules.title: Spending Money
quickRules.text: Children have almost no money of their own; teens can cover necessities for a few days; adults can buy what they need within reason. Only the Wealthy Strength lets you spend as a higher age bracket.

quickRules.title: Ages
quickRules.text: Children: +1 Flight and Charm, free Quick Healing, can't take Rebellious. Teens: +1 Fight and Brawn, free Rebellious. Adults: +1 Brains and Grit, free Skilled at… . Violence only between the same age bracket or within two years.

quickRules.title: Safety
quickRules.text: Road Signals (Brake, Backpedal, Coast, Pedal Harder) and the Detour list are always in play; anyone may use them at any time.

quickRules.title: Powered Character
quickRules.text: Introduced by the GM in the first session and co-controlled by everyone. The GM deals two Aspects per player; each player takes two and narrates when they're relevant (turn the card sideways). The GM also sets the Powered Character's Stats and a secret Fear. Players may add non-power Aspects; only the GM grants powers.

quickRules.title: Power Tokens
quickRules.text: The Powered Character has a pool of 7 PT. To use a power the GM sets a difficulty; spend 1 PT per d6 rolled, one at a time, adding results until you meet it or give up (spent PT are lost). A 6 is a Lucky Break: roll again and add. Each PT spent brings a GM-offered consequence, worsening with total PT spent.

quickRules.title: Power Difficulty
quickRules.text: Difficulty = Degree of Control (Low +1, Moderate +2, High +4) + Experience (Mastered +0, Practiced +2, Untried +4, Unconceived +6) + Deviation (Accelerating the Expected +0, Causing the Expected +1, Causing the Unexpected +2, Reversing the Expected +4, Causing the Impossible +6) + Scope (Tiny +1, Small +2, Medium +4, Large +6, XL +8, XXL +10).

quickRules.title: PT Consequences
quickRules.text: 1 PT: none or trivial. 2: minor physical. 3: minor mental. 4: significant physical. 5: significant mental. 6: profound physical. 7: profound mental. Beyond 7 (or into negatives) the GM decides, and effects outlast a night's sleep.

quickRules.title: Replenishing PT
quickRules.text: A full night's rest restores PT unless the pool hit zero or went negative — then recovery takes longer. One or two things (a food, sunlight, time with a bonded friend, a Banana Seat ride: up to 2 PT once per day) help them recover faster.

quickRules.title: Between Arcs
quickRules.text: Characters may gain a Knack or Bonded Action (narrate scenes showing it), gain or lose bike upgrades at the GM's discretion, and each player names one change in the town.
